rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent mass in all four views: a compact bar that bends and lifts into a stepped upper volume. The silhouette is legible and not overly fragmented, and the top/front/opposite views agree on the same dominant object, so it avoids the one-view-only failure. Parcel containment appears respected, and the geometry stays inside the green boundary without visible collisions. Programmatically, it can plausibly hold neighborhood living/commercial ground-up massing, but the visible ground response is weak: the blue access edge does not receive a clear court, notch, undercut, or public seam, so the street threshold feels sealed rather than active. The section is serviceable but somewhat generic; the upper bend/cantilever provides hierarchy, yet the mass does not strongly express a public ground condition or a clearly inhabited terrace/courtyard. Overall it is acceptable as an early massing with moderate program fit, but it needs a stronger access-facing void and a more legible active ground.
